content.label: Examiner note - why the acid must be nitric
content.body: Silver nitrate and barium chloride are added acidified to knock out carbonate or hydroxide ions that would give their own misleading precipitates. But the acid of record is dilute nitric acid: hydrochloric acid would add chloride ions of its own (a white precipitate before you even started) and sulfuric acid would add sulfate ions. Add the wrong acid and you test for your own reagent.
